title: 在残疾世界中生活成本高昂(5)
desc: 在残疾世界中生活成本高昂(5)

paragraphs.en: At times, I rally. At times, I believe that I am accepted and acknowledged.
paragraphs.zh: 有时，我会振作起来。有时，我相信自己被接纳和认可了。

paragraphs.en: I have the credentials, and the privileges, of a white male academic, living in a rich country, travelling with a passport that is all but universally valid.
paragraphs.zh: 我拥有白人男性学者的资历和特权，生活在一个富裕的国家，持有一本几乎全球通用的护照旅行。

paragraphs.en: At times, I can believe that my invisible work is, all things considered, negligible.
paragraphs.zh: 有时，我可以相信，综合考虑之下，我那些无形劳动微不足道。

paragraphs.en: That I am protected by the rights and the principles that were fought for over generations, that it is now merely an item of interest that I use a wheelchair.
paragraphs.zh: 我相信自己受到几代人争取来的权利和原则的保护，现在我使用轮椅仅仅是一件引人关注的事而已。

paragraphs.en: It felt like that as I planned for a sabbatical in California, as I was interviewed at the American embassy in Oslo, as I filled out the visa application that requested very specific information about my health, information that could be used to assess the level of risk I would pose to the public health and financial wellbeing of the United States.
paragraphs.zh: 当我计划去加利福尼亚州休假时；当我在奥斯陆的美国大使馆接受面试时；当我填写签证申请表，表格要求提供关于我健康状况的非常具体的信息，这些信息可用于评估我对美国公众健康和财政状况构成的风险程度时，我都有这种感觉。

paragraphs.en: As I glanced at the other people in the waiting room, many of whom did not have Norwegian passports or Norwegian privilege, it felt as though I was already on the inside, looking out.
paragraphs.zh: 当我扫视候诊室里的其他人时，他们中的许多人没有挪威护照，也没有挪威人所享有的特权，我感觉自己好像已经置身其中，在向外张望了。

paragraphs.en: And in California, in Berkeley, my family and I still felt ourselves to be in this privileged bubble.
paragraphs.zh: 在加利福尼亚州的伯克利，我和我的家人仍然觉得自己置身于这个优越的小圈子里。

paragraphs.en: Although our invisible work was redoubled in this foreign country, where we could not draw on the help of friends or family, where I had to strain to adjust to a house that was less accessible than our apartment back home, it still felt as though I could not be touched.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管在这个异国他乡，我们无形的劳动加倍了，在这里我们无法得到朋友或家人的帮助，我还得费力去适应一所不如家乡公寓方便的房子，但我仍然觉得自己好像不会受到影响。

paragraphs.en: That I was doing this thing – living abroad, as a wheelchair user, a guest of the University of California – that would have been impossible not so very long ago.
paragraphs.zh: 我正在做这件事——作为一名轮椅使用者，以加州大学访客的身份在国外生活——而就在不久前，这是不可能实现的。

paragraphs.en: It was January 2020 when we arrived.
paragraphs.zh: 我们是在2020年1月抵达的。

paragraphs.en: In February, it felt as if we had found our feet.
paragraphs.zh: 到了二月，感觉我们似乎已经站稳了脚跟。

paragraphs.en: As if we would soon be able to enjoy everyday life without a constant sense of strain, of always having too many unsolved tasks.
paragraphs.zh: 仿佛很快就能享受日常生活，无需持续感到压力，无需总是面对太多未解决的任务。

paragraphs.en: As if our invisible work was paying off. And then came March.
paragraphs.zh: 仿佛我们无形的努力正在取得回报。然后三月来了。

paragraphs.en: Along with the sudden sense of acute risk, of danger everywhere, came a redoubled workload.
paragraphs.zh: 随着突如其来的强烈风险感，以及无处不在的危险，工作量也加倍了。

paragraphs.en: With the kindergarten closed, with partly empty shelves at the supermarket, with public transportation gradually shutting down, every aspect of the day became a logistical challenge.
paragraphs.zh: 幼儿园关闭，超市货架部分空置，公共交通逐渐停运，日常生活的方方面面都成了后勤挑战。

paragraphs.en: From the day the pandemic became declared as such, on 11 March, we changed our minds constantly about staying or going, about whether we could manage.
paragraphs.zh: 自3月11日疫情被正式宣布以来，我们一直在纠结是留下还是离开，也不确定自己能否应对。

paragraphs.en: We'd hoped to stay until June, but in the end we caught the next-to-last plane leaving for Scandinavia from the east coast, on 28 March, the day I turned 39.
paragraphs.zh: 我们原本希望能待到6月，但最终在3月28日，也就是我39岁生日那天，我们搭上了从东海岸飞往斯堪的纳维亚半岛的倒数第二班飞机。

paragraphs.en: It wasn't only the work, of course.
paragraphs.zh: 当然，这不仅仅是工作的问题。

paragraphs.en: Fundamentally, it was the fear of closed borders, along with the fear of disease and death.
paragraphs.zh: 从根本上说，这是对边境关闭的恐惧，以及对疾病和死亡的恐惧。

paragraphs.en: But these fears were hard to disentangle.
paragraphs.zh: 但这些恐惧很难被分开。

paragraphs.en: I knew, with absolute certainty, that should I need to go to the hospital, my 180kg wheelchair would be left behind.
paragraphs.zh: 我确切地知道，如果我需要去医院，我那180公斤的轮椅将被留下。

paragraphs.en: Regardless of how my body would handle a Covid infection, I'd be helpless.
paragraphs.zh: 无论我的身体如何应对新冠病毒感染，我都将无能为力。

paragraphs.en: I knew, too, that should my wife need to go to the hospital, and I were left behind with our toddler, I would barely be able to cope without outside help – which was no longer to be had.
paragraphs.zh: 我也知道，如果我的妻子需要去医院，而我被留下照顾我们蹒跚学步的孩子，在没有外界帮助的情况下——而外界帮助已不复存在——我将几乎无法应对。

paragraphs.en: All over the world, many people had similar experiences.
paragraphs.zh: 在世界各地，许多人都有过类似的经历。

paragraphs.en: The rights, of course, were nominally in place – rights to services, rights to support.
paragraphs.zh: 当然，权利名义上是存在的——享受服务的权利、获得支持的权利。

paragraphs.en: But as disabled people across the world found out during the pandemic, the rights did not mean all that much when push came to shove.
paragraphs.zh: 但正如全球残疾人在疫情期间所发现的那样，到了紧要关头，这些权利并没有多大意义。

paragraphs.en: Not only did the rules of triage mean that during acute local crises, anyone with a chronic condition ran a higher risk of not receiving proper medical care, but the politics of the pandemic also meant that the physical needs of care went unmet – partly because resources were directed elsewhere, partly because public health measures could be invoked to dispense with services deemed too cumbersome or expensive.
paragraphs.zh: 分诊规则不仅意味着在局部严重危机期间，任何患有慢性病的人都更有可能得不到适当的医疗护理，而且疫情期间的政策也意味着护理的实际需求得不到满足——部分原因是资源被调配到了其他地方，部分原因是可以援引公共卫生措施来取消那些被认为过于繁琐或昂贵的服务。

paragraphs.en: As Lennard Davis put it, in an essay titled In the Time of Pandemic, the Deep Structure of Biopower Is Laid Bare: "In regard to disability, the ableism that puts on a compassionate mask in milder times now reveals its brutal face."
paragraphs.zh: 正如伦纳德·戴维斯在一篇题为《疫情时期，生命权力的深层结构暴露无遗》的文章中所说：“就残疾问题而言，在情况较好时戴着同情面具的能力主义，如今露出了其残酷的真面目。”

paragraphs.en: My family and I were very, very privileged.
paragraphs.zh: 我和我的家人都非常非常幸运。

paragraphs.en: We could pay for the plane tickets; we could go home.
paragraphs.zh: 我们买得起机票；我们可以回家。

paragraphs.en: Norway didn't exactly feel safe, but it felt infinitely safer than the US – and proved itself to be so over the time that followed, as the extreme vulnerability of disabled people became visible through sheer mortality rates.
paragraphs.zh: 挪威并不完全让人感到安全，但它感觉比美国安全得多——在接下来的时间里也证明了这一点，因为从死亡率中可以明显看出残疾人极其脆弱。

paragraphs.en: In crisis, the language of equal rights and anti-discrimination became that of utilitarianism and prioritisation.
paragraphs.zh: 在危机中，平等权利和反歧视的话语变成了功利主义和优先级排序的话语。

paragraphs.en: The invisible work did not become more visible.
paragraphs.zh: 那些无形的工作并没有变得更引人关注。

paragraphs.en: There was simply more of it, and even less justly divided than before.
paragraphs.zh: 只是这类工作更多了，而且分配比以前更不公平。

paragraphs.en: Economic inequality increased dramatically from March 2020 onward.
paragraphs.zh: 从2020年3月起，经济不平等现象急剧加剧。

paragraphs.en: So, perhaps, did moral inequality.
paragraphs.zh: 或许，道德层面的不平等也是如此。
